newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Demand may not boost gold - Newcrest.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Demand may not boost gold - Newcrest.

text.p: Growing demand for gold does not necessarily translate into a higher gold price, John Quinn, managing director of Australian mining house Newcrest Mining Ltd, said on Wednesday.

"There is no reason to believe that the worldwide demand for the yellow metal will not continue to be robust, in part because of expectation of high growth in Asia," Quinn told the Australian Gold Conference here.
"I do not think, however, that one can confidently predict this demand is going to result in any substantial rise in price," he said.
Mine production of gold remains strong as well and the intentions of central bankers are somewhat uncertain, Quinn said.
Central banks hold an estimated 35,000 tonnes of gold worldwide, analaysts forecast.
Meanwhile, data suggests average production costs among Australian mines in the third quarter of 1996 have increased to A$360 an ounce, he said.

"This represents an increase of nearly 10 percent on the costs reported for 1995 and is a continuation of a strongly upward trend in cash costs, which have been in evidence since the early 1990s," Quinn said.
Higher costs reflect higher fuel and processing and labor costs, he said.
A higher proportion of gold is being mined from more costly underground operations, Quinn said.
